name: Cerebras Inference API pricing - NEGATIVE: tier structure published, per-model token rates not in extracted page
region: Cerebras cloud (US); no regional GPU SKU to price
price_basis: NO price_usd recorded, deliberately. Cerebras publishes a two-tier STRUCTURE on the page - 'Cerebras Inference Tier Pricing' and 'Developer Tier Pricing' - plus a one-time $5 promotional credit for adding a payment method (expires 30 days after activation; API and Playground access pause when it expires or is exhausted unless PayGo credits are purchased separately; credit is non-transferable, no cash value, may be withheld). But the per-model per-1M-token numbers did not appear in the static HTML extraction on 2026-10-04, and no Cerebras GPU hourly rate is published. Writing down a remembered Cerebras per-token rate would be exactly the fabricated-price failure this repo's contract forbids.
notes:
An honest negative that still carries two usable facts. (1) The promotional-credit mechanic is a TRAP for benchmarking: $5 of free credit means the first few thousand requests run at an effective $0 rate, so a benchmark or cost projection run immediately after signup measures nothing about the real price. Price experiments only after the credit is exhausted, or on a paid tier. (2) Cerebras sells inference on its own WSE hardware at a scale where per-GPU-hour is not a purchasable unit - there is no hourly GPU price to compare a serverless rate against, which is precisely why the per-token rate there cannot be sanity-checked the way Fireworks' can. Cerebras is also listed as a routable provider on OpenRouter and Vercel AI Gateway, both of which add their own layer and their own markup.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04): NOT APPLICABLE IN THE HARDWARE-SHIPMENT SENSE - this record prices a token-based API, so no accelerator is transferred across a border and the ECCN 3A090 hardware licence regime does not attach to the transaction. Recorded null rather than false precisely because a token API is where export control instead becomes an END-USER/TERMS question: the provider applies geographic and end-user restrictions to service access (the AI Diffusion Rule briefly put a tiered country structure on exactly this kind of service before being rescinded on 2025-05-13), and a customer can still be refused under sanctions or end-use policy regardless of where the compute sits. Anyone reading this record for a restricted destination should look at the provider's terms, not at the EAR. Sources for the regime: spl-bis-2025-05-ai-diffusion-rescission, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance.

For a restricted destination, read the provider's terms, not the EAR. Sources: spl-bis-2025-05-ai-diffusion-rescission, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance.

 LEAD TIME: null - correct and not a gap. A token-priced serverless API is provisioned on request, so there is no lead time to publish; the binding constraint when a model is at capacity is provider-side queuing and any per-account concurrency limit, which this repo records in notes where a vendor publishes one (see the DeepSeek concurrency figures already here). Deliberately NOT recorded: any 'model capacity lead time' estimate, because vendors publish none and the SEO 'GPU lead time' numbers that circulate do not apply to a rented endpoint. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.

 ACCELERATOR LINK ADDED 2026-10-04: the hardware is Cerebras WSE-3 ([[accelerators/cerebras-wse-3]]), which is the whole reason per-GPU-hour is not a purchasable unit here - Cerebras sells inference on its own wafer-scale hardware at a scale where the accelerator is the system, so there is no per-GPU rate to compare a serverless token price against. That is the substantive fact this negative record carries, and it now points at the silicon record.
